title: A Slice of Warmth
story:
Sitting in the deep shadow of a wooden crate, James felt his heart hammering against his ribs. He closed his eyes to perform his grounding ritual, counting three distinct sounds to steady himself. One: the low, warm buzz of the yellow lantern overhead. Two: the soft, rhythmic scrape of leather boots on gravel. Three: the gentle, wheezing breath of the old human who had just sat down on the stoop nearby.

When James opened his eyes, the human was looking right at him. He was an older man with a beard like river foam and eyes that crinkled at the corners. He did not reach out to grab. He did not make a sharp, frightening noise. He did not chase James back into the dark. Instead, he simply sat in the pool of golden light, letting the silence stretch comfortably between them.

The man reached slowly into his woolen pocket and pulled out a small pocketknife and a round, bright red apple. With slow, deliberate movements, he carved a clean, crisp slice. The scent of the fruit cut through the heavy, metallic air of the town—a smell far sweeter than the oily puddles or the dry dust of the Whispering Flats, reminding James faintly of the high, sunlit fruit-boughs of the Great Canopy.

The old man held the slice out on his open palm, his hand steady and patient. James crept forward, his belly low to the damp cobblestones. He paused, looked up into the man's quiet eyes, and whispered his customary greeting: "Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next." He reached out, took the apple slice, and took a bite. It was cool, sweet, and tasted of morning. The old man smiled a slow, wrinkled smile, and the night suddenly felt a little less vast.
location: Under the lantern in the alleyway
